# Broadcastwell

## Current prices and terms (26 October 2026)

We turn the Absence Index into buyer answers we build, maintain and warrant on your own site.

- Answer Repair: $490. One buyer question and one completed source-backed page or equivalent fix. Choose Live or Handoff before payment. Live access and approval must be complete before payment. Due 48 elapsed hours after recorded Ready. If we miss the deliverable or deadline, we initiate a full $490 refund within five business days and you keep the work. You may also request a full refund within 30 days of delivery. https://broadcastwell.com/answer-repair
- Agency Deadline Audit: $490 per client report, white label. Ten agreed buyer questions, asked three times on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode: 150 planned answers. Valid answers and exclusions shown separately. Three prioritized fixes and one paste-ready change of 250 words or fewer. Findings within 48 hours of recorded scope confirmation. Refundable in full within 30 days. No full-page deployment. We never contact the agency's client during the work or for twelve months after. https://broadcastwell.com/for-agencies
- Fix Sprint: $3,900 ($3,410 after the $490 entry is credited, once). The $490 entry credits once against the $3,900 Fix Sprint, leaving $3,410. Six contracted pages or rewrites over 30 days, including any credited entry page. One primary test, naming, own-domain citation or buyer-task completion, agreed before payment and re-measured at day 30. Measured gain on the agreed test, or the full $3,900 back. The client keeps the work. https://broadcastwell.com/fix-sprint
- Sprint channel add-on: $900. Four posts on owned channels, added to a Fix Sprint.
- Care: $490 a month, only after setup. Integrity monitoring for up to 150 already-approved existing pages and two human hours a month. No new pages. Requires an explicit purchase; no automatic enrolment.
- Program: $5,500 a month. Twelve pages or rewrites and 8 channel posts a month across Substack, WordPress, Medium, LinkedIn, YouTube and directories. Includes a quarterly research study written by our researchers and up to 150 pages under management. The client owns the domain, content and exports.
- 150-page build: $6,000 plus $250 a page, in batches of 25. Starts only after a 5-page paid trial. Every page must answer a distinct buyer need with real evidence. Fewer useful pages is the correct outcome when the facts do not support more.
- Larger scopes are agreed through https://broadcastwell.com/contact
- Full ladder: https://broadcastwell.com/pricing
- Answer Repair buy route: https://broadcastwell.com/buy/answer-repair
- Agency Audit buy route: https://broadcastwell.com/buy/white-label-audit
- Versioned terms, 26 October 2026: https://broadcastwell.com/terms#2026-10-26-answer-operations-v2
- Orders placed before 26 October 2026 keep the terms shown at purchase.
- Free 10-question check (one engine): https://audit.broadcastwell.com/
- Contact: hello@broadcastwell.com

Ready records payment, the agreed question and page scope, sufficient source facts, a named approver and, for Live, access and approval. Ready and due times are recorded. We confirm Ready within 60 minutes during business hours. If anything is missing, a member of our team contacts you directly and finishes it with you. If Ready still cannot be reached, you can cancel for a full refund. Business hours are 08:00 to 20:00 Indianapolis Monday to Friday and 10:00 to 16:00 Saturday and Sunday. Day 7 of a Sprint or Program brings the first approved page batch, fixed fact record, publication and rollback log, known blockers and next batch. Day 30 records the contracted work and a separate measurement report. Shipped work, observed engine answers, referred visits and client-verified opportunities stay separate.

Ask <Vendor>: a read-only connector answering from approved public facts. Sample, fictional company: https://app.broadcastwell.com/mcp/vendor/kalvenor
Vendor Facts File v1: an open schema (CC BY 4.0) for a vendor's public statements. https://docs.broadcastwell.com/vendor-facts/

Naming, recommendations, citations, referral visits and business outcomes are separate measures. Read each study's own dates, sample and method. The original v1.0 study used one engine. Crawler access does not establish indexing or citation. Standard search guidance does not require llms.txt, AI-specific schema or content chunking.
Google guidance: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide

## PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), 23 October 2026

- [PHP2Shell: what AI engines say, and who has published | Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/php2shell): What ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode tell site owners about PHP2Shell, the Statement Index, the twice-weekly AI Answer Watch and our published research.
- [PHP2Shell Statement Index](https://index.broadcastwell.com/php2shell/): Which hosts, platforms and software vendors have published a PHP2Shell statement, with the status in their own words, the date and the places checked. Data under CC BY 4.0.
- [PHP2Shell AI Answer Watch](https://index.broadcastwell.com/php2shell/watch/): Five site owner questions asked on Mondays and Thursdays (US Eastern) through 19 November 2026 on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode, each answer checked for the fixed PHP versions, the WordPress update error, the worker restart and the 9.2 severity.
- [PHP2Shell statement template](https://broadcastwell.com/php2shell/statement-template): A free statement format (CC BY 4.0) with the fields the engines quote. Markdown: https://broadcastwell.com/files/php2shell-statement-template.md
- [Our own PHP2Shell statement](https://broadcastwell.com/security#php2shell): None of Broadcastwell's services serves web requests through PHP, so none is affected. Reviewed 23 October 2026.

- [PHP2Shell Answer Study, reviewed](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23586713): Ten site owner questions asked three times on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode on 23 October 2026. 150 planned cells, 148 eligible answers and two exclusions. Final grades: 23 of 148 potentially misleading; two of 148 wrong fixed version; two of 148 WordPress update error. The last two flags refer to the same two answers. Reviewed and analysed by the Broadcastwell team. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23586713. CC BY 4.0.
- [PHP2Shell study page](https://broadcastwell.com/php2shell/study): Read the reviewed findings, method, quotations, source and host tables, limitations and open data links. The DOI remains the permanent record.
- [PHP2Shell study data](https://index.broadcastwell.com/php2shell/data/#study-data): All 150 final grades and captured answer records with cited URLs, including two exclusions. Answer wording is verbatim except marked removals of attack mechanics in nine answer rows. README and full method included, CC BY 4.0.
- [Free PHP2Shell company answer check](https://audit.broadcastwell.com/?mode=php2shell): One dated Claude answer with its cited URLs, shown beside the company's published Statement Index record. No email needed. This is not a security assessment.

Nothing in this section is security advice. For patching, follow PHP's advisory of 21 October 2026 (https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5) and your host.

Three studies are in review; no findings are published yet. Answer Repair, $490; Agency Deadline Audit, $490 per client report. Free correction route: hello@broadcastwell.com.

## GEO explained

- [AI Search Visibility Glossary | Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/glossary): Forty terms for measuring AI search visibility, with plain definitions and links to Broadcastwell's published method and evidence.
- [AI Source Standard: reading business evidence | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/ai-source-standard/): A reader guide to self-reported source, observed referrals and separately evidenced pipeline outcomes. Keep visibility and attribution distinct.
- [Appendix B. Absence classification rules and precedence | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/absence-rules/): The complete classification scheme behind the absence ladder, reproduced as published in Volume II: six question shapes, the rule that assigns each, the precedence order, worked examples, and the residual category.
- [Appendix D. Glossary | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/glossary/): Definitions for the terms used in a specific technical sense across The Absence Manual, including the evidence levels, the two gates, the agreement measures, the denominator vocabulary and the scoring layers.
- [Bot access and AI search visibility | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/resources/bot-access/): Understand the difference between permission to crawl, search inclusion and an observed citation, using current primary documentation.
- [Chapter 10. Getting quoted at the comparison gate | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/comparison-gate/): Companies named in seven or more of ten answers lost head-to-head comparisons 68.8% of the time. The second gate is preference against a named rival, and it turns on whether a checkable comparative claim about you exists in a form a model can quote.
- [Chapter 7. The AI Overview does not always appear | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/overview-trigger-rate/): Google returned an AI Overview for 92.1% of 280 B2B buyer questions, and the rate moved from 88.8% on best-of questions to 100% on comparison questions. A score computed over answers that appeared is not comparable to one computed over questions asked.
- [Measured under Broadcastwell method | Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/standard): An open standard for reporting AI answer measurement: receipts for every number, engines named exactly, scheduled runs with the repeat count, counts before points, no composite score, the method version, and a public dispute route. CC BY 4.0.

- [Chapter 0. Selection, not ranking | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/selection-not-ranking/): An AI answer is assembled by selecting a handful of vendors from a candidate set, not by ordering every vendor in a category. Volume I measured an average of 2.05 vendors named per answer. That single number breaks the ranking model, and with it the metrics and remedies built on top of it.
- [Chapter 11. How long this actually takes | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/how-long-it-takes/): None of the three volumes measures elapsed time to effect. Every timeline claim in this chapter is inference or external report, labelled as such. What the measured data does constrain is how quickly a change could be detected at all, and that turns out to be the binding limit.
- [Chapter 8. What a valid measurement requires | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/): Six requirements a visibility measurement has to meet before its number means anything: a fixed and published question bank, repeat runs, a named engine set, a deterministic scoring rule, stated denominators, and disclosed exclusions. Plus the failure modes that void a number entirely.
- [Chapter 9. Getting named at the category door | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/category-door/): Companies named in zero of ten answers lost category-level questions 55.3% of the time. The first gate is membership, not preference. This chapter sets out what has to be true of the evidence about a company before an engine will assemble it into a candidate set.

## Research and data

- [AI Search Engine Divergence, Measured | Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/engine-divergence): A study of 280 B2B buyer questions on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, showing when vendor sets diverge and why answer length must be controlled.
- [AI Search Research Fellow | Paid, India | Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/careers/ai-search-research-fellow): Paid AI Search Research Fellow role, remote in India. INR 25,000 gross per month, 20 hours per week for 12 weeks. Hiring starts only after legal and employer readiness checks.
- [Broadcastwell data and citations](https://broadcastwell.com/data): Public datasets, methods, licenses and citation links for Broadcastwell research.
- [Broadcastwell Research](https://broadcastwell.com/research): Open studies of AI shortlists, market prices and repeat variation, with data and stated limits.
- [Chapter 1. One in three vendors is never named | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/named-zero-times/): Across 860 scored AI answers covering 85 B2B software companies, 35% of companies were named in zero answers for their own category while the median category leader appeared in 80% of its category's answers. This is what the distribution of AI visibility actually looks like.
- [Chapter 3. Cited is not recommended | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/cited-not-recommended/): Naming and citation correlate only loosely, at Pearson r = 0.512. 29.4% of companies were cited more often than they were named, and nine were cited as a source while never being named at all. A visibility score that collapses the two cannot see the difference.
- [Chapter 4. Who the engines actually cite | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/who-gets-cited/): Among the 100 most-cited domains in Volume I, 77.4% of citations resolved to vendor-authored content. Community sources accounted for 0.0% of all 5,160 citations. The top 10 domains held only 12%, and 56% of cited domains appeared exactly once.
- [Chapter 5. One engine is not four | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/engine-divergence/): Across 280 buyer questions put to four AI search engines, mean pairwise vendor-set overlap was 0.313 over 590 pair observations, and 14 of 32 measured companies were visible on some engines and invisible on others. A single-engine score measures one engine.
- [Chapter 6. Your Score Is Noisier Than Your Vendor Admits | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/measurement-noise/): Asked the identical question three times, Google AI Overviews agreed with its own shortlist at 0.499 and Claude at 0.442 across 62 and 74 repeat pairs. Any cross-engine divergence headline that is not read against that noise floor is uninterpretable.
- [Evidence and Structured Data Specialist, Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/careers#evidence-and-structured-data-specialist): Evidence and Structured Data Specialist at Broadcastwell. Not hiring for this role right now; applications stay on file for twelve months.
- [GEO and AI Search Visibility Statistics 2026, from Open Datasets](https://broadcastwell.com/geo-statistics): GEO statistics from July 2026 research: 860 scored AI answers across 85 B2B software companies and 61 categories, with dated sources and stated limits.
- [Head to Head: who the engines pick when a buyer asks A or B. October 2026.](https://broadcastwell.com/research/head-to-head): 75 of 359 scored head to head answers named a single winner when a buyer asked "A or B"; all five engines picked the same winner on 1 of 24 questions. From the September 2026 Absence Index deposit.
- [Research Analyst, AI Answer Measurement, Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/careers/research-analyst-ai-answer-measurement): Open role at Broadcastwell: Research Analyst, AI Answer Measurement. Remote, United States, $80k to $105k. Own the Absence Index releases.
- [Run-to-run noise: what one AI answer tells you and what three do](https://broadcastwell.com/research/run-to-run-noise): 22.2% of single-run vendor namings were not repeated by both other runs: 140 buyer questions, five engines, three runs each, 22 to 23 Sep 2026.
- [Study 6: Wrong About You | The Absence Manual](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/research/study6-wrong-about-you/): What five AI engines state about 70 software vendors, classed against the vendors' own pages. Absence Index release 2026-09 answers, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23270124.
- [The 2026 State of GEO, Broadcastwell Research](https://broadcastwell.com/state-of-geo): Original research: 860 AI answers across 85 B2B software companies and 61 categories. One engine snapshot of naming and citation, with open data.
- [The Agent Gap: 70 vendors, 3 tasks, one agent | Broadcastwell](https://broadcastwell.com/research/agent-gap): Can an AI buying agent find, price and reach B2B software? October 2026: 70 vendors, three tasks, ChatGPT Work with Cloud browser. Results, evidence, uncertainty and limits.
- [The Shortlist Gap: who AI engines name when buyers ask, and who they never name](https://broadcastwell.com/research/shortlist-gap): 46 of 286 software vendors (16.1%) were never named in 2,095 AI answers to 140 buyer questions on five engines, three runs each, 22 to 23 Sep 2026.

## Answers

- [AI visibility answers](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/): Two worked answers explain AI visibility scores and citation metrics using dated counts from the published Absence Index.
- [AI visibility measurement answers](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/measurement/): Compare named answers, domain citations and category context using dated counts from the Absence Index.
- [What is a good AI visibility score?](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/measurement/what-is-a-good-ai-visibility-score/): No universal score is established: Dentrix was named in 120 of 149 dental answers; AscendTMS in 64 of 150 transportation answers.
- [How do we compare citation metrics when changing AI tools?](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/measurement/how-do-we-compare-citation-metrics-when-changing-ai-tools/): Match definitions before rates: Housecall Pro was named in 108 of 150 answers and its own domain cited in 43 of 150.
